title: Kingdom of Kongo founded
description: Lukeni lua Nimi founds a kingdom with its capital at Mbanza Kongo that comes to rule both banks of the lower Congo.

title: Diogo Cão reaches the Congo
description: The Portuguese navigator sets up a stone pillar at the river's mouth and makes the first contact with the Kingdom of Kongo.

title: Baptism of the king of Kongo
description: Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised as João I, beginning the long Catholic tradition of the Kongo court.

title: Luanda founded
description: Paulo Dias de Novais founds São Paulo de Luanda, which becomes the capital of the colony and a leading port of the Atlantic slave trade.

title: Benguela founded
description: The Portuguese found a second colony in the south, later a major slave port.

title: Nzinga becomes queen of Ndongo
description: Nzinga Mbande succeeds her brother and for almost forty years leads Ndongo and Matamba against Portuguese expansion.

title: Dutch capture Luanda
description: A Dutch West India Company fleet takes Luanda and allies with Kongo and Nzinga against the Portuguese.

title: Portuguese retake Luanda
description: An expedition from Brazil under Salvador Correia de Sá drives out the Dutch.

title: Battle of Mbwila
description: A Portuguese army defeats and kills King António I, and Kongo falls into decades of civil war.

title: Fall of Pungo Andongo
description: The Portuguese take the last stronghold of the kings of Ndongo and end the kingdom.

title: Kimpa Vita burned
description: The prophetess who had led a mass movement to restore the kingdom of Kongo is executed for heresy.

title: Bailundo revolt
description: The Ovimbundu of the central highlands rise against traders and forced labour and are defeated, completing Portuguese control of the plateau.

title: Diamang founded
description: A company with exclusive rights begins mining diamonds in the north-east and runs the region almost as its own territory.

title: Benguela Railway completed
description: The line from the port of Lobito reaches the Congo border, carrying the copper of Katanga to the Atlantic.

title: MPLA founded
description: Nationalist groups merge into the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola, the party that later governs the country.

title: UNITA founded
description: Jonas Savimbi founds a third nationalist movement, based among the Ovimbundu.

title: Alvor Agreement
description: Portugal and the three nationalist movements agree on independence and a shared transitional government, which collapses within months.

title: Independence
description: Portugal withdraws, the MPLA under Agostinho Neto proclaims the People's Republic in Luanda, and the civil war between the movements continues.

title: Attempted coup of Nito Alves
description: A faction of the MPLA tries to seize power, and thousands are killed in the purge that follows.

title: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
description: Angolan and Cuban forces fight South African and UNITA forces to a standstill in the largest battle in Africa since 1945.

title: Tripartite Accord
description: Angola, Cuba and South Africa agree on the withdrawal of Cuban troops from Angola and the independence of Namibia.

title: Bicesse Accords
description: The government and UNITA sign a ceasefire and agree to hold multiparty elections.

title: Election and return to war
description: The MPLA wins the first multiparty election, UNITA rejects the result, and the civil war resumes more destructively than before.

title: Lusaka Protocol
description: A second peace agreement brings a partial ceasefire that breaks down in 1998.

title: Death of Jonas Savimbi
description: Government troops kill the UNITA leader, and a ceasefire six weeks later ends twenty-seven years of civil war.

title: João Lourenço becomes president
description: José Eduardo dos Santos steps down after thirty-eight years as president.
